sector: An independent arts and culture quarterly, published four times a year around one long photo essay and its writing.
founded_place_size: Published by Lumen House Press, a two person imprint in Portland, Maine, founded 2016.
about: Lumen Quarterly is a print magazine about art, craft and the people who make things along the coast. Each issue turns on one photo essay and about two thousand words of reporting. Readers pay for it because it is good to hold and worth keeping on a shelf, not for news.
audience: Design literate readers aged 30 to 55 who buy the object as much as the article and renew a subscription because the magazine is made with care.
price_positioning: Eighteen dollars a single copy, sixty dollars a year. An independent object priced above a newsstand title and below an art book, sold on typographic craft rather than volume.
typography: The whole product is the type. A refined display serif for the masthead and openers, a readable book face for the two thousand word body at a generous measure, a quiet sans for captions, credits and folios. Real hierarchy, white space the eye rests in.
voice: Considered, warm and exact, written like an essay rather than a pitch. Example line the brand would write: He has built the same hull the same way for forty years, and he still stops to look at the grain before the first cut.
brand_assets_status: The house style guide was made by the magazine's first designer, who has left, and it is now a couple of issues out of date on type. The masthead artwork inside the guide is a flattened screenshot, so the only proper record of the wordmark is the printed cover, which has been scanned. The printer also returned last season's press file.
values: Every issue should feel like the same magazine. Continuity of type, measure and picture treatment is the identity, and the reader should recognise Lumen before reading a word.
